newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Italian freed after Christmas eve kidnapping.
newsitem.headline: Italian freed after Christmas eve kidnapping.

text.p: An Italian businessman kidnapped on Christmas eve in a town on Venezuela's border with Colombia was rescued on Friday in a joint operation by Colombian and Venezuelan police, authorities said.

Colombian police said Clemente Antonio Passariello, 51, whose kidnappers had demanded $400,000 in exchange for his release, was snatched back from his abducters in a rural area on the outskirts of San Cristobal, just across the border from Colombia's northeastern city of Cucuta.

Three Venezuelans and one Colombian, suspected of carrying out the kidnapping on behalf of leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels, were arrested in a raid on the site where Passariello spent his 25-day kidnap ordeal, police said.
Colombian police said they did not know Passariello's hometown in Italy or the exact nature of his business activities.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, is known for kidnappings and the protection of rural drug operations.
